parole.significato: pocket (pouch in clothing for storing items)
parole.testo: Probably from ki̇̀šti (“to poke, to shove”) + -enė. Older theories have suggested that the word may instead have been borrowed from Slavic; compare Belarusian кі́шка (kíška), Polish kiszka (“intestine, bowel”), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *kyšьka.
Likely a Slavic borrowing, from Proto-Slavic *sěra. Cognate with Latvian sȩ̄̃rs.
Of Slavic origin, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *višьňa. Compare Polish wiśnia (“sour cherry”), Belarusian ві́шня (víšnja, “sour cherry”) and Ukrainian ви́шня (výšnja, “sour cherry”).

parole.significato: Jew (member or descendant of the Jewish people)
parole.testo: From a Slavic language (probably Belarusian жыд (žyd) or Polish żyd), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *židъ.
